command: g l | g q | g c | g d | g x | g z | g w
name: Loki drive jumps (custom)
description: this machine's prepend_keymap: g + key hops to a WSL drive/dir

examples.note: → /mnt/q/Codings/ClaudeCodeProjects/LEX (the LEX project)

examples.cmd: g q / g c / g d / g x / g z
examples.note: → Q:/C:/D:/X:/Z: drives (mounted at /mnt/<letter> in WSL)
→ ~ (WSL home)

explanation: Defined in ~/.loki-term/yazi/keymap.toml as prepend_keymap, so it overrides defaults. On native Linux the /mnt paths don't exist, so these are harmless no-ops.

examples.note: next / previous file (or ↓/↑)
h = up to parent dir, l = enter the selected dir (or ←/→)
jump to top / bottom of the list

name: directory history back/forward
description: step back and forward through visited directories

examples.note: back to the previous directory
forward again

name: select files
description: toggle selection or enter visual selection mode

examples.note: toggle selection on the current file and move down
visual mode: extend selection as you move
visual UNSET mode: drag to deselect

name: copy, cut, paste
description: yank or cut the selection, then paste into the current dir

examples.note: copy selected files, paste into the dir you navigate to
cut (move) instead of copy
paste with overwrite of existing files

explanation: Selection persists across directory changes, so yank here → navigate → paste there.

name: trash or delete
description: d moves to trash (recoverable); D deletes permanently

examples.note: send selected files to the system trash
permanently delete — no trash, no undo

gotchas: D is irreversible; prefer d unless you're sure

name: create / rename
description: create a new file or dir, or rename the selection

examples.note: create a file; end the name with / to create a directory instead
rename the current file (or bulk-rename a multi-selection)

explanation: a + 'name/' makes a directory; a + 'name' makes a file.

name: toggle hidden files

examples.note: flip show_hidden (default off in this config)

explanation: Default is show_hidden=false (set in yazi.toml); this toggles it for the session.

name: find within the listing
description: jump-to-name search inside the current directory

examples.note: find next matching name; ? finds backward
repeat the find forward / backward

explanation: 'find' just moves the cursor to matching names in the CURRENT dir — for a recursive search use s or S.

name: recursive search (fd / ripgrep)
description: search files by name (fd) or by content (ripgrep)

examples.note: search file NAMES recursively via fd
search file CONTENT recursively via ripgrep

gotchas: needs fd and ripgrep installed on PATH

name: filter the listing
description: live-filter the current directory to names matching a pattern

examples.note: type to narrow the visible files; <Esc> clears the filter

explanation: Filter hides non-matching entries in place (unlike find, which only moves the cursor).

name: open files
description: open with the default app, or pick the opener interactively

examples.note: open with the configured default opener
open interactively — choose which program to use

name: run a shell command
description: run a shell command in the current directory

examples.note: run a shell command (non-blocking)
run a blocking shell command (waits, shows output)

explanation: Use $0, $@ etc. to reference hovered/selected files in the command.

examples.note: create a new tab in the current directory
jump straight to tab N
previous / next tab
swap the current tab with the previous / next

name: copy path to clipboard
description: copy the file's path/name to the system clipboard

examples.note: copy the full path (file URL)
copy the directory path
copy the filename
copy the filename without its extension

name: quit yazi
description: exit, optionally without writing the cwd file

examples.note: quit (writes cwd-file so a shell wrapper can cd there)
quit WITHOUT writing the cwd-file — stay in the original dir

explanation: The 'yy'/shell-wrapper that cds-on-exit relies on q writing --cwd-file; Q opts out of that.
